llm.summary: This is a disclosed security monitoring suite with persistent options, but the risky behaviors are purpose-aligned and gated by user-directed setup or confirmation.

dimensions.detail: The skill’s stated purpose is advisory monitoring, signature verification, guarded installs, and security-skill management; the observed scripts and hook implement those functions without hidden exfiltration or destructive behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The triggers include broad phrases such as 'update skills' and 'verify skills', which could activate the skill for generic security requests, but artifact instructions still route changes through setup commands or approval-gated flows.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Manual installation downloads release artifacts, verifies signatures and checksums, then replaces the existing clawsec-suite directory; this is disclosed and scoped to the intended install path.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network access to advisory/catalog sources and local reads of installed skill metadata are proportionate for advisory matching; feed fetching is signed by default and includes domain restrictions in the hook feed loader.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The hook and optional cron job are persistent host-side automation, but they are clearly documented, installed only by explicit setup scripts, and the hook writes state and alerts rather than deleting or disabling skills.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a security suite that can add an OpenClaw hook and optional recurring cron scan. Review the hook/cron setup before running those scripts, keep signed-feed verification enabled, and treat broad skill-update requests carefully because this package can guide install and security-management workflows.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Shell commands, network fetches, local writes, and persistence are disclosed in SKILL.md and skill.json runtime/operator-review metadata, so this is a disclosure note rather than a policy concern.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Some trigger phrases are broader than ideal for a security suite, especially 'update skills', but no artifact evidence shows automatic mutation from trigger activation alone.
[RA2] expected: Persistent hook and optional cron setup are intentional, documented, scoped to OpenClaw security monitoring, and non-destructive by default.
[RA1] unexpected: The broad 'update skills' trigger is over-scoped, but the guarded installer checks advisories and requires explicit second confirmation when advisory risk is present.
[staticScan:suspicious.install_untrusted_source] expected: The static hit appears to come from embedded advisory-feed text describing an SSRF example URL, not from an install source used by the skill.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean and did not add negative evidence.
